examples.text: Ich lächle und sage: »Bitte, kommen Sie doch herein.« (...) Charlotte, meine Assistentin, kommt dazu, nimmt ihm den Mantel ab, kümmert sich, wuselt, plappert, bietet Getränke an, versprüht Charme – all die Dinge, für die ich sie bezahle.

examples.text: Der plappert viel dummes Zeug, wenn der Tag lang ist.

translations.source_sense_description: aus Freude am Reden fröhlich vor sich hin erzählen

glosses: To utter words indistinctly or unintelligibly; to utter inarticulate sounds

examples.text: The men were babbling, so we couldn't make sense of anything.

glosses: To talk incoherently; to utter meaningless words.
To talk too much; to chatter; to prattle.

examples.text: She babbled on for hours about the importance of some new gadget.
Radical rather than rhetorical, babble like an oracle

glosses: To make a continuous murmuring noise, like shallow water running over stones.

examples.text: Hounds are said to babble, or to be babbling, when they are too noisy after having found a good scent.
In every babbling brook he finds a friend.

glosses: To utter in an indistinct or incoherent way; to repeat words or sounds in a childish way without understanding.

examples.text: All this vvhile John had conn'd over ſuch a Catalogue of hard VVords, as vvere enough to conjure up the Devil; theſe he uſed to babble indifferently in all Companies, eſpecially at Coffee-houſes; ſo that his Neighbour Tradeſmen began to ſhun his Company as a Man that vvas crack'd.

glosses: To reveal; to give away (a secret).
Idle talk; senseless prattle

examples.text: This is mere moral babble.

glosses: Inarticulate speech; constant or confused murmur.

examples.text: [M]an has an instinctive tendency to speak, as we see in the babble of our young children; whilst no child has an instinctive tendency to brew, bake, or write.

glosses: A sound like that of water gently flowing around obstructions.

examples.text: [T]he babble of the stream / Fell, and without the steady glare / Shrank the sick olive sere and small.

translations.source_sense_description: aus Freude am Reden fröhlich vor sich hin erzählen

glosses: Talk, especially meaningless or unimportant talk.

examples.text: Although hardly coming under my theme, I cannot omit this: "Against a woman's chatter: Taste at night fasting a root of radish, that day the chatter cannot harm thee."

glosses: The sound of talking.
The vocalisations of a Eurasian magpie, Pica pica.
The vocalisations of various birds or other animals.

examples.text: The hare cried and complained of the terrible February cold and the disgusting chatter of the owls[.]

At dawn and at sunset the howler monkeys screamed together and the parakeets broke into shrill chatter, but during the hot hours of the day only the full drone of insects, like the beat of a distant surf, filled the ear, while nothing moved amid the solemn vistas of stupendous trunks, fading away into the darkness which held us in.
The wind rose as the earth darkened, so that fading chatters of woodland animals were countered by the strengthening sounds of waving trees […]

glosses: An intermittent noise, as from vibration.

examples.text: Proper brake adjustment will help to reduce the chatter.

glosses: In national security, the degree of communication between suspect groups and individuals, used to gauge the degree of expected terrorist activity.

examples.text: The NSA is concerned about increased chatter between known terror groups.

glosses: The situation where a drill or similar tool vibrates and tears the material rather than cutting it cleanly.
To talk idly.

examples.text: They knitted and chattered the whole time.
That teacheth trickes eleuen and twentie long, / To tame a ſhrew, and charme her chattering tongue.

glosses: To make a noise by rapid collisions.

examples.text: He was so cold that his teeth were chattering.

glosses: To utter sounds which somewhat resemble language, but are inarticulate and indistinct.

examples.text: The jay makes answer, as the magpie chatters with delight.

Is your cat intently staring out the window at a bird on a branch and “chattering” in a kind of shaky, high-pitched, breathy way? If so, she is expressing excitement at what she's observing (or maybe the desire to attack what she sees as prey).

glosses: One who chats.
A user of chat rooms.

examples.text: During the chat sessions, two outreach team members would engage in a conversation about the topic chosen for that event in the main chat room and entice other chatters to join in.

translations.source_sense_description: aus Freude am Reden fröhlich vor sich hin erzählen

glosses: To talk rapidly, indistinctly, or unintelligibly; to utter gibberish or nonsense.

examples.text:
1829, James Hogg, The Shepherd’s Calendar, New York: A.T. Goodrich, Volume I, Chapter 9, “Mary Burnet,” p. 184,
Allanson made some sound in his throat, as if attempting to speak, but his tongue refused its office, and he only jabbered.
“What are you jabbering about, shipmate?” said I.

The noise of their battle with Numa had drawn an excited horde of savages from the nearby village, and a moment after the lion’s death the two men were surrounded by lithe, ebon warriors, gesticulating and jabbering—a thousand questions that drowned each ventured reply.

glosses: To utter rapidly or indistinctly; to gabble.

examples.text: She had Lord James' collar in one big fist and she pounded the table with the other and talked a blue streak. Nobody could make out plain what she said, for she was mainly jabbering Swede lingo, but there was English enough, of a kind, to give us some idee.
He wept very little, but when he wept he howled aloud, and jabbered wild abuse, threats and recriminations through the wet torrent of his howling.

glosses: Rapid or incoherent talk, with indistinct utterance; gibberish.

examples.text:
1735, Jonathan Swift, Gulliver’s Travels, in The Works of Jonathan Swift, edited by George Faulkner, Dublin, 1735, Volume 3, A Letter from Capt. Gulliver to his Cousin Sympson, pp. v-vi,
And, is there less Probability in my Account of the Houyhnhnms or Yahoos, when it is manifest as to the latter, there are so many Thousands even in this City, who only differ from their Brother Brutes in Houyhnhnmland, because they use a Sort of a Jabber, and do not go naked.

Two tongues from the depths,
Alike only as a yellow cat and a green parrot are alike,
Fling their staccato tantalizations
Into a wildcat jabber
Over a gossamer web of unanswerables.

Mark Pauline has a good line of gab, in his elliptical, left-handed fashion. He's at relative rhetorical ease with classy theoretical jabber such as emergent behavior, cyborganics, chaos theory, transparent interfaces, artificial life, and the machinic phylum.

glosses: One who or that which jabs.

examples.text: Have the boys box, one jabbing and the other practicing the methods of boxing a jabber.

glosses: One who administers a hypodermic injection.

examples.text: Like Claire, these “secret jabbers” are keeping it private even from their closest family and friends.

glosses: A kind of hand-operated corn planter.

examples.text: The jabber was the most popular hand-operated corn planter ever devised. […] Inset shows jaws closed for jabbing (left) and open for depositing kernels (right).

translations.source_sense_description: aus Freude am Reden fröhlich vor sich hin erzählen

glosses: To talk casually; to discuss unimportant matters.

examples.text: What are you guys nattering about? You're clearly not following the meeting!

glosses: To nag.
Mindless and irrelevant chatter.

translations.source_sense_description: aus Freude am Reden fröhlich vor sich hin erzählen

glosses: To talk fast, idly, foolishly, or without meaning.

examples.text: Does she regard him simply as a workman come to do a job for her, someone whom she need never lay eyes on again; or is she gabbling to hide discomfiture?
I pitied thee, took pains to make thee speak, taught thee each hour one thing or other; when thou didst not, savage, know thine own meaning, but wouldst gabble like a thing most brutish
Then he fell to gabbling strange and dreadful things which were not clearly understandable.
Americans are always drinking in crossroads saloons on Sunday afternoon; they bring their kids; they gabble and brawl over brews; everything’s fine.

glosses: To utter inarticulate sounds with rapidity.

examples.text: gabbling fowls
I not to Cinna’s Ears, nor Varus dare aſpire; / But gabble like a Gooſe; amidſt the Svvan-like Quire.

glosses: Confused or unintelligible speech.

examples.text: a lot of gabble from witnesses
[T]he driver was delayed there by a skimpy little woman with a thin piping voice practised in the art of defeating escape from it by a ceaseless stream of gabble.

translations.source_sense_description: aus Freude am Reden fröhlich vor sich hin erzählen

glosses: Empty or silly idle talk or writing; nonsense, rubbish.

examples.text: You're talking a load of twaddle. Get your facts straight, man!
"What ineffable twaddle!" I cried, slapping the magazine down on the table; "I never read such rubbish in my life."
I would rather be rude than to listen to twaddle from a man I’ve known.

It was her other self who had written that letter. It not only bored, it rather disgusted her real self. "Flippant and silly," said her real self. Yet she knew that she'd send it and she'd always write that kind of twaddle to Nan Pym.
I improvised for three or four minutes, speaking complete twaddle in character.

glosses: One who twaddles; a twaddler.
To talk or write nonsense; to prattle.

examples.text: To Edward […] he was terrible, nerve-inflaming, poisonously asphyxiating. He sat rocking himself in the late Mr. Churchill's swing chair, smoking and twaddling.

translations.source_sense_description: aus Freude am Reden fröhlich vor sich hin erzählen

glosses: To speak incessantly and in an inconsequential or childish manner; to babble.

examples.text: And as E. Rushmore Coglan prattled of this little planet I thought with glee of a great almost-cosmopolite who wrote for the whole world and dedicated himself to Bombay.

I looked across at Anna, and I noticed that her eyes had grown strangely blank, without expression. I felt instinctively that the subject brought up by Victor was one she would not have chosen. Victor, insensitive to this, went prattling on.

glosses: Silly, childish talk; babble.

examples.text: Mere prattle without practice is all his soldiership.

examples.text: На подоконнике сидел и болтал ногами в джинсах совершенно незнакомый дядька.

examples.text: За рулём она вечно болтала без умолку, напоминая Нике жителя Чукотки, который едет на оленях по бескрайней тундре и поёт нескончаемую песню обо всем, что попадается ему по дороге.

examples.text: Патрульные были заняты — они болтали с хорошенькой продавщицей пива.
